answers.reasoning: setState runs the updater, Object.is-compares the result to current state, then captures previousState and applies the replace-or-merge assignment before notifying listeners
useStore passes api.subscribe unchanged plus two inline snapshot readers, () => selector(api.getState()) and () => selector(api.getInitialState()), to the plain useSyncExternalStore
an explicit replace argument takes precedence (true=wholesale, false=merge); only when omitted does it fall back to type-based behavior (non-object/null assigns, object merges shallowly)

pre-React-18 zustand hand-rolled the subscription with useReducer/forceUpdate plus refs that re-checked state right after subscribing to avoid zombie children; PR #550 swapped that for the use-sync-external-store shim, and #2301 later moved to calling React.useSyncExternalStore directly
create() builds the vanilla store then Object.assign(useBoundStore, api) copies setState, getState, getInitialState and subscribe onto the hook as own properties
